notes:
Phantom-free fit (post-io_callback refactor).

**This JSON was edited by hand, not refit.** Two primitives (psiG_cache, Lq_rep) were dropped without rerunning NNLS. The MoS2 3x3 DoE that produced this fit had those coefficients at 1.0 each, but:

* ``psiG_cache = n_k * n_b * n_s * n_r / P`` counted the resident ψ(G) cache.  After the io_callback refactor ψ(G) lives on host — no such device-resident buffer exists.  Dropping removes an extrapolated ~3.3 GB/process phantom at Si 10^3 scale.

* ``Lq_rep = n_k * n_rmu^2`` was a residual absorber.  HLO audit of Si 10^3 fit_one_rchunk confirmed NO c128[n_k, mu, mu] fully-replicated buffer exists — L_q is c128[n_k, mu/p_x, mu/p_y] throughout.  At the MoS2 3x3 DoE scale this primitive was exactly collinear with Lq_sharded (fixed P=4); NNLS assigned it coef=1 as a phantom.  Dropping removes another ~3.7 GB/process extrapolation error at Si 10^3.

Remaining primitives:
* pair=4: 4 concurrent pair-density temps at ZCT peak — fact-based (P_l + P_r + P_l_Rt + P_r_Rt with donation at worst case).
* centroid=9: residual-absorber, ~30 MB/process at DoE scale, scales with n_k * mu * n_b * n_s / p_x.  Not physically clean but keeps total within ~5%.

Expected behavior: at MoS2 3x3 (training scale) total prediction drops by ~130 MB (small).  At Si 10^3, total drops by ~7 GB (big), finally matching post-io_callback AOT measurements.

TODO: rerun the DoE AT POST-IO_CALLBACK SCALE with a multi-node variation so NNLS can separate Lq_sharded/Lq_rep properly and centroid residual can be attributed.  Until then this hand-edited fit is strictly a conservative upper bound — it loses the phantom terms but keeps the centroid residual absorber, so predictions stay within ~5% of AOT at the validated test points (MoS2 3x3, Si 10^3).
